llm_proposer.assessment: The outage of svc230 is most likely part of a network-wide optical failure at the common ROADM S06, specifically failure of a WSS input port. The simultaneous multi-channel OCH losses and loss of input at two different outgoing S06 line amplifiers favor a common optical blocking point over a client, transponder, span, or OTN-layer fault.

proposals.rationale: Every affected working path depends on roadm.S06, and a failed WSS input port there can block all channels arriving on the common degree before they fan out toward multiple outgoing lines, matching the simultaneous OCH_LOS and S06-originating AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms. The main uncertainty is that no explicit WSS equipment alarm is shown.
proposals.note: the element's equipment does not document the mode

proposals.rationale: A disconnected common optical input near S06 could also remove all channels and cause downstream input-loss alarms. It is less likely because a single ordinary OMS connector would normally affect one section, whereas losses are seen on multiple S06 egress lines.

A switch-fabric failure at the common site could interrupt many ODUs simultaneously. However, an OTN-layer failure should not cause widespread OCH_LOS or amplifier input-loss alarms, so the optical evidence argues strongly against it.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode
